findings.title: Cron-line field layout and the "root" user are hard-coded in several places
findings.description: `production_lines` filters host lines with `j.split()[5] == "root"`. `main()` in `cutover_227_tick_backup.py` reads the cron user with `production_lines(...)[0].split()[5]`. `_JOB_LINE` encodes the same five-schedule-field layout a third time. The literal `"root"` and index `5` also live in the cron template and in the test helper `_host_block`, which matches `" root "`. The project rule says a value used in comparisons is defined once. One named constant or parsed-line type, such as a `CronJob` dataclass holding `user` and `command`, would stop these copies from drifting apart. Also, `main()` takes the first production line to be the cron user's line. That holds only while line order is stable, and nothing checks it.

findings.title: `assert` used for runtime narrowing in production code
findings.description: `assert match is not None` and `assert flags is not None` in `run_health` are control-flow guards. Under `python -O` they vanish, and the failure becomes an `AttributeError` or `TypeError` with no step context. In an operator cutover tool that records expected against seen, these should raise `StepFailed` explicitly or be restructured so the type checker needs no assert.

findings.title: Tests for the provisioning script assert source text instead of behavior
findings.description:
Several new tests regex-extract assignments and functions from `provision_tick_cluster.sh` and compare them with literal strings:
- `test_parent_directories_755_data_directory_700`
- `test_only_trading_tick_is_created`
- `test_roles_are_applied_with_replication`, which asserts that a substring appears in the function body
- `test_roles_sql_grants_replication_only_when_asked`, which only checks the order of two substrings in the SQL

These break on harmless reformatting and would still pass if the logic were wrong. `test_hba_admits_*` is better, since it executes `hba_content`. The replication-grant tests should run `provision_tick_roles.sql` against a throwaway database, as the existing role tests apparently do. That is the only way to prove REPLICATION is conferred only with the flag.

findings.title: Cutover script and tests loosen the strict typing and import conventions
findings.description:
- `sys.path` is mutated before imports, with `# noqa: E402` on every import.
- The tests type the `ctx` fixture and helper parameters as `Any`, and load modules by file path, which defeats strict pyright.
- `cutover_227_tick_backup.py` is about 320 lines, a little over the ~300-line guideline.

I could not confirm that `[tool.ruff.lint]` and `[tool.pyright]` are present in `pyproject.toml`, or that pyright is clean on `scripts/`. Packaging `scripts/` as a module would remove the path hack, and a typed `Context` return would remove most of the `Any` uses.

findings.title: The lifecycle check swallows the helper's exit status and inspects only its output text
findings.description: `b2_lifecycle.sh` failures are turned into `MISSING <cluster> lifecycle-read` by parsing the text. If the helper dies before printing anything, for example from a usage error or a missing `jq`, the output is empty. The `while read` loop then runs once on an empty line and reports `lifecycle-read` with a blank detail. The failure is still counted, but the cause is lost. `b2_lifecycle.sh` also does not check that `jq` and `rclone` exist before using them. Capture the exit code and include stderr in the report.

findings.title: Bash design in `render_cron.sh` and `b2_lifecycle.sh`
findings.description:
- The quoted replacement strings in the `${x//pat/"rep"}` substitutions correctly guard against bash 5.2 `patsub_replacement` mangling `2>&1`, and `test_ampersand_survives_substitution` pins that behavior.
- Cluster blocks are inserted before the common placeholders are substituted, so `@CHECKOUT@` and the like still resolve inside them.
- Refusing unfilled placeholders and an unescaped `%` is retained.
- `b2_lifecycle.sh` is read-only by design, and the comment explains why rclone's `lifecycle` set would replace every rule. That is a sound guard.
- `grep -v '^##'` under `set -e` and `pipefail` would abort the render with no message if the cluster template ever contained only `##` lines. This is unlikely, but it would be easy to handle explicitly.

findings.title: Operator-facing scripts follow the repo's check-then-act conventions
findings.description:
- The failure handler in `run_steps` catches specific exception types at a process boundary, records them, and stops. That fits the project's exception rule.
- The restart step refuses to restart production and re-checks tick advisory locks immediately before restarting.
- No credentials appear in the source, and the application key reaches rclone only through its environment.
- The test fixture for the cron parser uses the real pre-227 installed file, which meets the real-format parsing rule. I could not confirm the fixture's contents.

structured_findings.summary: Cron-line field layout and the "root" user are hard-coded in several places
`assert` used for runtime narrowing in production code
Tests for the provisioning script assert source text instead of behavior
Cutover script and tests loosen the strict typing and import conventions
The lifecycle check swallows the helper's exit status and inspects only its output text
Operator-facing scripts follow the repo's check-then-act conventions
